subject: Follow-up: DPA & SCC selection for ACME Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: DPA & SCC selection for ACME Health

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed: 

- Redwood is happy to move forward on the DPA and SCC selection to support ACME Health’s GDPR review.
- Confirmed questions for alignment: data roles (controller vs processor), desired SCC modules, and whether you need a BAA/HIPAA assurances for any PHI flows.
- You mentioned sending over ACME’s vendor security questionnaire — we'll have our security team complete that.

I’ve attached our standard DPA template and a short SCC module selection matrix to help accelerate selection. Rishi (copied) will attach our SOC 2 report and confirm HIPAA posture.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm ACME’s role (controller) and Redwood’s role (processor) for the planned integration.
2) Share the vendor security questionnaire (if you haven’t already).
3) Let us know which SCC module you prefer; if you’re unsure, we can recommend an option based on controller vs processor alignment.
4) If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with Rishi to walk through the security artifacts and any redlines.

Timeline goal: sign DPA within 2–3 weeks so procurement can proceed.

Attachments:
- Redwood_DPA_template_20270715.pdf
- SCC_module_matrix_20270715.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA & SCC selection for ACME Health

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — very helpful. A few notes from our side:

- ACME Health will be the controller for patient and customer data; Redwood will be the processor for the inference requests.
- We do require SCCs for EU data transfers; we generally use the standard processor module. I’ve attached our vendor security questionnaire — can your security team fill and return?
- We’ll need a SOC 2 Type II report; does Redwood have a recent one you can share?
- We may need HIPAA BAA language for any PHI flows; can Rishi advise on whether Redwood can sign a BAA for hosted deployments or if that requires Private deployment?

Attached: ACME_Vendor_Questionnaire.docx

If you can send the SOC report and recommended SCC selection, I’ll route to procurement for review. If we can get the DPA signed in the next 2–3 weeks that would work for our timeline.

Best,
Tom Reynolds
Senior Procurement Manager, ACME Health
tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA & SCC selection for ACME Health

Hi Tom / Marissa —

Thanks for the context. Quick answers from security: 

1) SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II report for the period ending 2027-06-30. I’ve uploaded a redacted copy to a secure share here: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/secure/SOC2-202706 (link sent to procurement/security). Attachment stub: SOC2_report_redwood_202706.pdf. If you need an unredacted copy we can arrange an NDA first.

2) HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workflows in our Dedicated and Private deployment options. For our hosted API, we can discuss contractual assurances; however, a full BAA for hosted multi-tenant service typically requires additional controls or a Dedicated/Private deployment. Happy to scope options once we understand volumes and flows.

3) SCC selection recommendation: Since ACME is the controller and Redwood is the processor, we recommend selecting the SCC processor module (processor-to-controller clauses) and including the standard supplementary clauses that cover onward transfers and subprocessors (see attached SCC_module_matrix_20270715.xlsx). If procurement prefers, we can accept the controller-to-processor template with a processor annex — our legal team is flexible on how the clauses are mirrored.

4) Vendor questionnaire: We’ll complete ACME_Vendor_Questionnaire.docx and return within 3 business days.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to send DPA to procurement for initial review (done).
- Security to fill questionnaire and supply redacted SOC2 (we will).
- Procurement to confirm SCC module choice or we provide a recommended default (processor module).
- If BAA is required, flag here so we can evaluate Dedicated/Private options and get legal involved.

Attachments: SOC2_report_redwood_202706.pdf (redacted); SCC_module_matrix_20270715.xlsx

Happy to join a call with your security/procurement team this week — Marissa, can you propose 30 min slots?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 17:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA & SCC selection for ACME Health

All —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the SOC2 link. Confirming ACME’s preference is to use the processor SCC module. Procurement will review the DPA and SCC matrix; I’ve asked Sara (cc’d, security lead) to review the SOC2 redacted report and our questionnaire responses.

Next steps from ACME: procurement will return any redlines on the DPA within 5 business days. If we need an unredacted SOC2 or an NDA first, Sara will flag.

Marissa — could you propose 30-min windows tomorrow or Tuesday for a short review call with Sara and myself? We’ll aim to finalize SCC selection + DPA redlines on that call.

Thanks,
Tom
